_meta.status: DRAFT — AI-drafted from the rule's context, test and official text; not yet human-reviewed

kinds.missing: every target must be present and is absent
kinds.missing-any: at least one of the targets must be present; none is. When the targets carry a `group`, at least one per group must be present ("the seller's VAT ID or tax number, and the buyer's VAT ID"); a field result keeps its group
kinds.invalid: the target is present but its value is wrong (format, code list, checksum)
kinds.forbidden: the target is present but not allowed in this combination
kinds.inconsistent: the fields disagree. In a calculation the result is the target (it is what the rule checks, and recomputing it always satisfies the rule) and the inputs are operands; in a comparison with no derived side (dates, codes that must match), every field is an operand
kinds.structural: the XML breaks a rule the simplified JSON cannot express (a duplicated, empty or malformed element). Any sender's invoice can trip it; our own generator never should, so `generator` says why and a hit on a document we generated is a bug. Fields point at the nearest data
kinds.unrepresentable: concerns XRechnung-extension structures the simplified JSON has no fields for; the note has to carry the whole message

_meta.anchored: a field with "anchored": true applies only on the anchor's branch: it keeps the matches the anchor is, lies inside, or contains (the document itself excepted); a containing anchor must supply every ~. index, or it would widen to every item. For a rule that fires on different kinds of object, each target names its own

roles.condition: a field whose value made the rule apply
roles.operand: an input of a calculation, or one side of a comparison with no derived side

conventions.no rule-set conditions: BT-24 (and anything else that only selects which rule set runs, e.g. $isCVD) is never a condition: every rule in the set already presupposes it
conventions.narrowest field: map the field the rule tests, not its group; the group is a path prefix any consumer can walk up to. Map a group only when its entries are what is tested ("exactly one entry such that …"), and then with a filter
conventions.schema, not generator: fields name what the simplified-JSON schema can hold; what an editor shows of them is a UX question
conventions.anchor: `anchor` accepts what check_anchors.py reports for the rule (a collision, an unbound ~., a relative path off the schema), and says why it does no harm
conventions.notes: `note` is shown to the person checking the invoice, whoever sent it: plain words, no BT codes. `generator` says why our own generator can't (or rarely does) trip the rule; `remark` is for whoever maintains this table. Neither is shown

paths.syntax: JSON Pointer patterns (@facturion/pointer-patterns, SPEC.md): a JSON Pointer (RFC 6901) is a pattern matching itself
the list index of the finding's anchor at this position; no anchor there → every item
paths.~*: every item, regardless of the anchor
paths.~?f=v: the entries whose member f equals 'v'; none matching → the list itself, as the place to add one
paths.~?f!=v: the entries whose member f is a string other than 'v'; none matching → nothing
paths.~?a~1b=v: a nested member: the entries whose a/b equals 'v' (~1 separates the steps)
paths.~?!f: the entries without member f (missing or null; an empty string counts as present); none → nothing
paths.unmatched filters: only a target's unmatched ~?f=v means "add one here"; a condition's or operand's yields nothing
paths.0/x: relative to the finding's anchor (Relative JSON Pointer; 0 = the anchor itself)

BR-DE-5.note: XRechnung requires a contact at the seller: a person's name or a department.
BR-DE-5.remark: CII also accepts DepartmentName; the simplified JSON only has contact.name.

BR-DE-14.note: Every VAT breakdown row has to state its rate, even when it is 0 %, as for exempt or reverse-charge amounts.
BR-DE-14.generator: The generator always writes a Percent (rate or 0), so in practice this cannot fire from our JSON.

BR-DE-19.note: The payment is a SEPA transfer, which needs a valid IBAN, and this account number isn't one. Only a warning, but a payment to it may fail: check it for typos, or for a national account number where the IBAN belongs. If the number shown is a valid IBAN, the invoice files it as another kind of account number (possible in CII only), and the sender has to correct that. If a card is marked instead, the invoice labels its card payment as a SEPA transfer, which it can't be: the sender has to correct the payment type.
BR-DE-19.remark: The JSON has one means code for all means, so a card block carries the transfers' code 58 and the rule fires on it too; `anchored` keeps the transfer target off the card's finding and the card off a transfer's.
BR-DE-19.generator: CII: the generator writes accounts shorter than 14 chars or not starting with two letters as ProprietaryID, so the IBAN check sees an empty IBANID.

BR-DE-22.note: Two attached files have the same file name. XRechnung requires every attached file to have a name of its own; rename one of them.
BR-DE-22.remark: Fires on the root, so it cannot say which documents collide; a UI could compute that from the data.

BR-DE-25-a.note: The payment is marked as a SEPA direct debit, so the invoice has to carry the direct-debit details: the mandate reference and the account to be debited.
BR-DE-25-a.generator: UBL tests for cac:PaymentMandate, which the generator only writes when mandate_reference is set; without it the whole direct debit (incl. debited account) is dropped from UBL.

BR-DE-27.note: The phone number should contain at least three digits. Only a warning. If there is no phone number at all, this appears together with the missing-phone error, and adding one fixes both.
BR-DE-27.remark: Fires when the phone is absent too (regex against the empty string), alongside BR-DE-6.

BR-DE-28.note: The e-mail address doesn't look valid: it needs exactly one @ with at least two characters on either side, and no dot right next to the @ or at either end. Only a warning. If there is no e-mail address at all, this appears together with the missing-e-mail error, and adding one fixes both.
BR-DE-28.remark: Fires when the e-mail is absent too, alongside BR-DE-7.

BR-DE-30.note: A SEPA direct debit needs the creditor identifier of the seller (or of the payee, if someone else collects the payment).
BR-DE-30.remark: UBL carries BT-90 as a SEPA-scheme PartyIdentification on the seller or payee, not inside PaymentMeans.

BR-DE-TMP-32.note: The invoice should say when the goods or services were supplied: a delivery date, an invoicing period, or a period on every line. A period on only some of the lines isn't enough.

BR-DE-CVD-03.note: A clean-vehicle invoice needs at least one line that carries both the vehicle category classification and the 'cva' attribute. Having them on different lines isn't enough.

BR-DE-CVD-06-a.note: A line with the vehicle category classification needs exactly one 'cva' attribute: none and two are both errors.
BR-DE-CVD-06-a.remark: Requires exactly one 'cva' attribute, so it also fires on two; the filter then marks both.

BR-DE-CVD-06-b.note: A line with the 'cva' attribute needs exactly one vehicle category classification: none and two are both errors.
BR-DE-CVD-06-b.remark: Requires exactly one CVD classification, so it also fires on two; the filter then marks both.

BR-TMP-3.note: The gross price and the net price of this line state different base quantities or units; XRechnung requires them to match. The editor holds one base quantity per line, so it can show only one of the two. Check the line's price with the sender.
BR-TMP-3.generator: CII only. The schema holds one base quantity (BT-149, a single element in EN 16931); CII writes it under both the gross and the net price, and the generator writes the same value to both. Gross price is a condition: without it CII has no second base quantity.

BR-TMP-4.note: This supporting document has more than one description; XRechnung allows one. Only a warning, but the editor shows just one of them.
BR-TMP-4.generator: CII only. The JSON has one description per document.

BR-TMP-5.note: This supporting document carries more than one attached file; XRechnung allows one per document. Only a warning, but the editor shows just one of them.
BR-TMP-5.generator: CII only. The JSON has one attachment per document.

BR-TMP-6.note: A date is not written as year-month-day (YYYY-MM-DD). Only a warning, but the date may have been read wrongly: compare it with the sender's PDF or ask them.
BR-TMP-6.generator: UBL only. Fires on the date element itself; the JSON schema already enforces YYYY-MM-DD.

BR-TMP-7.note: A date is missing its format marker or is not written as YYYYMMDD. Only a warning, but the date may have been read wrongly: compare it with the sender's PDF or ask them.
BR-TMP-7.generator: CII only. The generator always writes format="102".

BR-DEX-01.note: This attachment's file type isn't allowed. Besides the usual types (PDF, images, spreadsheets, CSV), the XRechnung extension also allows XML.

BR-DEX-02.note: This invoice uses sub-lines, an XRechnung extension that groups lines under a parent line. A line's amount should equal the sum of its sub-lines. The editor can't show sub-lines, so the error can't be pointed at a field; check the line amounts against the sender's PDF.

BR-DEX-03.note: This invoice uses sub-lines, an XRechnung extension that groups lines under a parent line, and a sub-line is missing its VAT information. The editor can't show sub-lines, so the error can't be pointed at a field; ask the sender for a corrected invoice.

BR-DEX-04.anchor: The only place `0/scheme_id` can't resolve is the SEPA creditor ID (a plain string in the JSON), and the rule's test allows SEPA on the seller and payee, so it never fires there.
BR-DEX-04.note: The scheme code of this identifier isn't on the ISO 6523 list XRechnung allows (0088 for a GLN, for example). Check the code, or ask the sender for it.

BR-DEX-05.note: The scheme code of this identifier isn't on the ISO 6523 list XRechnung allows (0088 for a GLN, for example). Check the code, or ask the sender for it.

BR-DEX-06.note: The scheme code of this identifier isn't on the ISO 6523 list XRechnung allows (0088 for a GLN, for example). Check the code, or ask the sender for it.

BR-DEX-07.note: The scheme code of this electronic address isn't on the list XRechnung allows (EM for an e-mail address, 0204 for a Leitweg-ID, for example). Check the code, or ask the sender for it.

BR-DEX-08.note: The scheme code of the delivery location's identifier isn't on the ISO 6523 list XRechnung allows (0088 for a GLN, for example). Check the code, or ask the sender for it.

BR-DEX-09.note: This invoice uses third-party payments, an XRechnung extension for amounts collected on someone else's behalf. The amount due doesn't add up once they are included. The editor can't show third-party payments; check the amount due against the sender's PDF.

BR-DEX-10.note: This invoice uses third-party payments, an XRechnung extension for amounts collected on someone else's behalf, and one of them has no payment type. The editor can't show third-party payments; ask the sender for a corrected invoice.

BR-DEX-11.note: This invoice uses third-party payments, an XRechnung extension for amounts collected on someone else's behalf, and one of them has no amount. The editor can't show third-party payments; ask the sender for a corrected invoice.

BR-DEX-12.note: This invoice uses third-party payments, an XRechnung extension for amounts collected on someone else's behalf, and one of them has no description. The editor can't show third-party payments; ask the sender for a corrected invoice.

BR-DEX-13.note: This invoice uses third-party payments, an XRechnung extension for amounts collected on someone else's behalf, and an amount has more than two decimal places. The editor can't show third-party payments; ask the sender for a corrected invoice.

BR-DEX-14.note: This invoice uses third-party payments, an XRechnung extension for amounts collected on someone else's behalf, and an amount is in a different currency than the invoice. The editor can't show third-party payments; ask the sender for a corrected invoice.

BR-DEX-15.note: This invoice seems to use sub-lines (lines grouped under a parent line). XRechnung doesn't support them in this format, and the editor can't show them. Only a warning, but check the line amounts against the sender's PDF.

PEPPOL-EN16931-R001.note: The invoice has to state the business process it belongs to; for PEPPOL billing that is urn:fdc:peppol.eu:2017:poacc:billing:01:1.0.
PEPPOL-EN16931-R001.generator: The XRechnung profiles default ProfileID, so only an explicitly empty override could trigger it.

PEPPOL-EN16931-R008.note: The invoice contains a field with no value in it. That rarely changes what the invoice says, but it makes the invoice invalid; the sender's software should leave out fields it has nothing to put in.
PEPPOL-EN16931-R008.generator: The generator skips empty values; firing means a field slipped through as an empty string.

PEPPOL-EN16931-R010.note: XRechnung requires the buyer's electronic address, where the invoice is delivered: for public buyers usually the Leitweg-ID, otherwise often an e-mail address.
PEPPOL-EN16931-R010.remark: No BT code in the text; matched by name ("Buyer electronic address" = BT-49).

PEPPOL-EN16931-R020.note: XRechnung requires the seller's electronic address, where the buyer can reach the seller electronically, often an e-mail address.
PEPPOL-EN16931-R020.remark: No BT code in the text; matched by name ("Seller electronic address" = BT-34).

PEPPOL-EN16931-R043.note: This allowance or charge doesn't say whether it reduces or increases the total. Ask the sender which one is meant before booking the invoice.
PEPPOL-EN16931-R043.generator: ChargeIndicator is derived from which list the entry sits in.

PEPPOL-EN16931-R043-1.note: This allowance or charge doesn't say whether it reduces or increases the total. Ask the sender which one is meant before booking the invoice.
PEPPOL-EN16931-R043-1.generator: CII document/line allowances and charges; ChargeIndicator is derived from which list the entry sits in.

PEPPOL-EN16931-R043-2.note: The price adjustment on this line doesn't say whether it is a discount or a surcharge. Ask the sender which one is meant before booking the invoice.
PEPPOL-EN16931-R043-2.generator: CII price-level allowance; the generator always writes false.

PEPPOL-EN16931-R044.note: This line's price includes a surcharge. XRechnung allows only discounts on the price itself; a surcharge belongs on the line as a charge. The editor can't show a price surcharge, so the line's price may look different from the sender's PDF.
PEPPOL-EN16931-R044.generator: The JSON can only express a price-level allowance (discount), never a charge.

PEPPOL-EN16931-R053.note: The invoice states its VAT total more than once. It's unclear which figure applies; ask the sender for a corrected invoice.
PEPPOL-EN16931-R053.generator: The generator writes exactly one TaxTotal with subtotals.

PEPPOL-EN16931-R054.note: The invoice names a separate currency for VAT accounting, so it also has to state the VAT total in that currency.
PEPPOL-EN16931-R054.generator: The second TaxTotal (BT-111) is only written when the caller supplies it; BT-6 without BT-111 trips this.

PEPPOL-EN16931-R101.note: This line refers to a document. XRechnung allows a line to reference only an identifier for the invoiced object, such as a meter or contract number; other line-level references aren't shown in the editor.
PEPPOL-EN16931-R101.generator: The generator only writes line document references with type 130.

PEPPOL-EN16931-R120.note: The line's amount doesn't equal its quantity times its price, plus its charges and minus its discounts. Only a warning, and often a rounding difference, but check which figure is right.
PEPPOL-EN16931-R120.generator: The generator computes BT-131 itself, so this only fires through rounding in the inputs.

PEPPOL-EN16931-R121.anchor: CII states the base quantity under both the gross and the net price; the JSON holds one, so both places are the same field.

PEPPOL-EN16931-R130.anchor: CII states the base quantity under both the gross and the net price; the JSON holds one, so both places are the same field.
